newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - May 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - May 14.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Announcing the first interim profit since the January merger of St George Bank Ltd and the Advance Bank yesterday, St George managing director Jim Sweeney unveiled aggressive new cost-cutting targets. The bank recorded a 12 per cent rise in net profit to $83.7 million and is now targeting savings from the merger of A$175 million a year. Page 1.

According to the Global Equity Investment Review, United States institutions have rediscovered the Australian sharemarket, largely due to a push by US pension funds to invest offshore. The study showed US holdings of Australian shares increased in value by US$3.3 billion in 1996. Page 1.

After closing more than 20 plants in the past 12 to 18 months and implementing changes to cut costs by at least A$100 million a year, directors of paper and packaging giant Amcor warned yesterday that earnings in this half-year would continue to fall from the depressed levels of the past year, dropping profits for the 1996-97 year to a six-year low. Page 19.

New Zealand's Carter Holt Harvey has attributed a 45 per cent drop in full-year earnings, with a net profit of NZ$251 million for the 12 months to March, to weak pricing in its wood and forest product business, a 43 per cent decline in pulp prices, and wek Japanese and Korean economies. Page 19.

General insurer MMI Ltd yesterday announced its third Asian venture - a three-way joint venture with Alpic Finance and Allianz AG designed to tap into India's health insurance market and eventually its general insurance industry. MMI international operatins general manager Angus MacIver said yesterday progression of the deal to the insurance licence stage would depend on the Indian Government's approval. Page 21.

The consolidation for the first time of the historic 105-year-old Coolgardie goldfield in Western Australia has underpinned a record production period for sole owner Herald Resources Ltd, which now plans to stabilise production at about 115,000 ounces a yar after its first quarter as owner. Page 24.
THE AUSTRALIAN

As financial markets expressed their disappointment that the Federal Budget's underlying deficit did not fall closer to its expected A$2 billion, investors dumped the dollar and sold bonds last night, with key bond futures prices falling about eight points, pushing yields higher. Page 41.

While Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry chief executive Mark Paterson said last night's Federal Budget laid the framework for stability and GDP growth to exceed 3.75 per cent in 1997-98, the lack of initiatives for industry disappointed business groups. Page 41.

The Howard Government is relying less on business investment this year to underpin its Budget predictions for 1997-98, forecasting growth of eight per cent, half the bullish 16 per cent predicted and achieved in 1996, with the Treasury commentary accompanying the Budget saying the continued growth in business spending reflects the positive influences on investment. Page 41.

Under tax changes announced in last night's Federal Budget aimed at wealthy individuals requiring changes to the Income Tax Amendment Act, the Government has moved to crack down on private companies that lend funds to associated parties under non-commercial arrangements. Page 43.

Despite the announcement of savage cuts to its funding in the 1996-97 Budget, the Australian Securities Commission is expected to see income from the regulation of companies and securities jump by 9.6 per cent in 1997-98. The ASC budget for the regulation of companies will fall 6.2 per cent under the Budget to A$95.1 million in 1997-98. Page 43.

Budget papers released last night have revealed the Federal Government has issued present and some former Telstra directors and executives indemnity against any legal proceedings arising from the scoping study for its impending privatisation or an Australan Securities Commission investigation. Page 43.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Superannuation experts criticised Federal Treasurer Peter Costello's announcement last night that the Government would introduce a 15 per cent rebate on savings accounts, superannuation contributions and a broad range of other investments, with Association of Superannuation Funds of Australia executive director Susan Ryan saying the move would confuse most savers. Page 25.

Financial markets reacted negatively yesterday to the higher-than-expected projected underlying Federal Budget deficit in 1997-98 of A$3.9 billion, with market traders selling bonds, the dollar, and sharemarket futures immediately after its announcement. Page 25.

Paper and packaging group Amcor has warned of falling second-half profits because of weak paper prices and shrinking margins, with the company possibly forced to write up to A$160 million off the value of its offshore assets. The news sent Amcor's share price down from its day's high of A$8.75 to A$8.45, or 18 cents down on the day. Page 27.

Rumours that Crown Casino shareholders Kerry Packer and Carlton and United Breweries are looking to sell their substantial holdings has contributed to a 9.6 per cent drop in Crown's share price since the day its permanent casino opened in Melbourne. Crown shares have fallen from A$2.25 last Wednesday to yesterday's A$2.07. Page 27.

Woolworths managing director Reg Clairs announced yesterday the retail giant had arranged an A$800 million syndicated loan with nine major international and Australian banks as part of its push into the wholesaling and petrol station markets. Clairs said the money would go towards the construction of new distribution centres and petrol rollout. Page 27.

New South Wales-based St George Bank recorded a 12.3 per cent increase in net profit for the six months to March, with net profit after preference share dividends higher-than-expected at A$83.7 million, including a two-month contribution of A$19.1 million from Advance Bank. The Bank warned earnings would be slow in the second half because of intense pressure on home lending. Page 27
THE AGE

As details of the Federal Budget were released yesterday, yields on November 2006 interest rate bonds rose to 7.70 per cent and the dollar weakened as overseas investors sold it down. Financial markets and business leaders labelled the Budget "uninspiring", saying Federal Treasurer Peter Costello had missed a prime opportunity to boost industry and invigorate the economy. Page B1.

Large companies and professional investors will be hit after Federal Treasurer Peter Costello unveiled a range of measures, including moves to protect dividend streaming, designed to protect the Government's tax revenue base. The moves also include a crackdown on deals that pass imputation tax credits on dividends from those that cannot claim them to those that can. Page B1.

David Perry, of Austock Brokers, has predicted that the proposed mega-merger between Guinness and Grand Metropolitan could lead to a shake-up at Inntrepeneur, the A$1 billion British pub chain that Grand Met jointly owns with the Foster's Brewing Group, wth either party selling, or with Inntrepeneur being floated. Page B1.

The Federal Government has taken direct control of tax deductions on infrastructure projects, with the Budget including a new low-cost tax incentive scheme aimed solely at road and rail projects. Federal Finance Minister John Fahey confirmed yesterday the Coalition believed general infrastructure investment no longer required special Government assistance. Page B1.

After reporting profits of A$140 million in the December half-year, Amcor surprised the market yesterday with another warning that trading conditions had failed to improve, while prices for some paper-based products had deteriorated even further. The company's failure to meet profit targets in many of its paper and packaging divisions may see it face assets writedowns this year of well over A$100 million. Page B3.

Under a deal announced yesterday which will add to Energy Developments' success in Australia, where it operates 200MW of capacity, the Melbourne-based independent energy producer has won the right to build power plants fired by landfill gas at six sites in the United Kingdom. Page B3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
